transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-08-09
Start time: 15:00 PT
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Alicia Ramos (Redwood AE), Marcus Lee (Redwood SE), Priya Shah (Nebula Head of ML), Daniel Brooks (Nebula SRE), Karen Liu (Nebula Security)
Recording id: ff-20260809-8347

Summary: quick console walkthrough focusing on tracing, error analysis and request logs to validate debugging flows and guardrails for a production pilot. Customer has strict latency SLOs and SOC2 requirements; they want to understand hosted vs dedicated tradeoffs and how request logs / trace correlation helps root-cause incidents.

Topics: tracing UI, error analysis, request logs export, KV cache visibility, model fallbacks, dedicated capacity latency guarantees, security controls (KMS/SSO/audit logs)

Transcript:
[00:00] Alicia Ramos: hey everyone thanks for joining, we'll kick off in a second. uh curious — Priya you mentioned some high level goals in the calendar, do you want to re-state them quickly?
[00:12] Priya Shah: yeah sure, thanks Alicia. main things for us: 1) we run real time summarization and customer support routing so latency needs to be sub 250ms p95 ideally, 2) we need detailed logs and traces for audits and debugging, and 3) we can't send PCI data to third-party persistent storage — so we are evaluating VPC/on-prem or redwood dedicated.
[00:30] Alicia Ramos: perfect, that gives us a good frame. Marcus will run through the console — tracing and request logs — then we'll show how error analysis ties into alerts and runbooks.
[00:40] Marcus Lee: cool. share screen — ok i'm in the console, quick note, some names in the UI may read as "Redwood Console" or sometimes our internal metric labels show up as rwd-trace which is our shorthand, sorry for any confusing labels.
[00:55] [00:55] Marcus Lee: first, tracing. you can see each request collects a trace id and you can expand spans — we automatically attach model variant, region, latency per-stage, batch size. here's an example request that hit a fallback to a smaller quantized variant, notice the cross-region fallback at the end.
[01:20] Daniel Brooks: the fallback — does that change semantics? if we fall back to a smaller quantized model are we looking at a different tokenization behavior or quality drop?
[01:30] Marcus Lee: great question. generally small quant variants keep same tokenizer and model family but you can see a small BLEU-like drop in some test prompts; the console surfaces a delta score in the error analysis tab so you can quickly see regressions. sometimes the transcription will show "quantize" as "quanteyes" — ignore typos in auto labels.
[01:48] Priya Shah: can tracing correlate to our internal request ids? we have an internal correlation id for each customer request.
[01:55] Marcus Lee: yes — you can pass your correlation id as metadata and it becomes a top-level column in request logs and is searchable, we also support log forwarding to your own SIEM using the webhook export.
[02:10] Karen Liu: about data residency — where are request logs stored for hosted? are they retained by default?
[02:18] Alicia Ramos: hosted retention defaults to 30 days in the console, but for Dedicated and Private we give you retention controls and you can configure S3 export or disable persistent logs. we'll include the SOC2 security pack with the export procedures.
[02:33] [02:33] Marcus Lee: moving to error analysis — this section groups errors by exception type, e.g., API timeouts, model OOM, malformed prompts, and it shows a sample request with stack trace. here's a cluster that spiked during a high concurrency window — you can filter by route, model version, and customer id.
[02:58] Priya Shah: what counts as an "error" in your system? are soft failures where model returns hallucinated content flagged?
[03:06] Marcus Lee: currently we flag infra and API errors automatically. for quality errors like hallucinations we integrate with Redwood Optimize — you can feed prompt-based evals and set regression alerts; the console will flag changes to metrics like factuality, hallucination rate.
[03:24] Daniel Brooks: latency — can we see per-stage timings? e.g., scheduling, KV cache lookup, model forward?
[03:32] Marcus Lee: yep. each span includes scheduling latency, batch wait, kv-cache hit vs miss, token generation. note that KV cache is sometimes shown as k v cache in the transcript if your speech-to-text chops the acronym.
[03:47] [03:47] Speaker 1: (inaudible)
[03:52] Marcus Lee: here's a request with a high batch wait — you can set SLO alerts for batch wait > 40ms. and you can also configure routing policies to prefer low-latency pool, or fall back to cheaper pool if cost is prioritized.
[04:10] Priya Shah: for our use case cost is important but latency is primary. how does dedicated help vs hosted?
[04:18] Alicia Ramos: Dedicated gives you reserved GPU capacity and predictable p95s — we provide config examples in the deck. hosted can be bursty during peak but we have tiered capacity and intelligent routing. we'll send the latency SLA table.
[04:31] Karen Liu: are audit logs and KMS integration available for dedicated? we need HSM integrations for key material.
[04:40] Alicia Ramos: yes, Dedicated and Private support customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM and audit log forwarding. we'll attach the integration guide.
[04:48] [04:48] Marcus Lee: switching to request logs UI — you can query by trace id, correlation id, model_version, metadata fields. exports are CSV/ndjson and also direct S3 delivery for dedicated accounts.
[05:05] Daniel Brooks: ndjson export — does it include full token-by-token outputs or is that redacted?
[05:11] Marcus Lee: token-level outputs are redacted by default; you can opt-in for full transcript exports in dedicated/private with appropriate security attestation.
[05:22] Priya Shah: that policy is good. we also need to obfuscate PII automatically — does the console do that?
[05:28] Marcus Lee: yes we have redaction options and PII scrubbing rules you can customize — the console shows a redaction preview.
[05:36] [05:36] Speaker 2: small lag on the screen —
[05:38] Marcus Lee: apologies — network hiccup.
[05:44] Marcus Lee: diving into debugging flows — let's simulate an incident: high 500s on route /summarize. you can click into traces to see that the model forward stage had repeated OOMs and then a fallback to a smaller model. the error analysis aggregates affected users and gives a suggested runbook like "increase worker pool" or "pin to dedicated pool".
[06:06] Priya Shah: can the console integrate with our PagerDuty?
[06:10] Marcus Lee: yes we support webhooks and PagerDuty/Slack integrations; alerts can include trace links and a pre-filtered request log sample.
[06:18] Daniel Brooks: for debugging we need preserved request logs for 90 days. is that possible?
[06:24] Alicia Ramos: with Dedicated you can set longer retention and ship to your S3; for hosted we can offer enterprise retention add-on. we'll include options in the pricing doc.
[06:36] [06:36] Priya Shah: quick question about model rollouts — if we do a canary and it fails quality checks does console auto rollback?
[06:44] Marcus Lee: you can set automated rollback on quality regressions tied to prompt sets in Redwood Optimize. console will show a canary funnel and regression stats, and you can auto-rollback or route traffic away.
[06:58] Karen Liu: is there RBAC for console access? we need read-only for some auditors and write access limited to platform team.
[07:06] Alicia Ramos: yes full RBAC and SSO (SAML/OIDC) — we'll include an access matrix.
[07:12] [07:12] Marcus Lee: now open the request logs query — example query: model_version:"redwood-rw1" AND response.status:500 AND metadata.customer_id:nebula-finance | sort by timestamp.
[07:28] Priya Shah: okay that query looks good. can we save queries and attach them to alerts?
[07:33] Marcus Lee: yes you can save queries and reference them in alerting rules.
[07:36] [07:36] Speaker 3: (laughs)
[07:40] Marcus Lee: moving on — sample benchmark section, we have a shared spreadsheet (link: https://redwood.ai/benchmarks/nebula-sample) where we'll record p95 numbers across model variants and quantization profiles.
[07:56] Daniel Brooks: we'll share sample corpus and a list of typical prompts. Priya will send that.
[08:02] Priya Shah: yes I'll upload a 50k prompt set and expected SLOs.
[08:08] Marcus Lee: great. a couple notes on batching — the runtime will automatically batch similar requests but you can configure max batch latency; the console shows batch decomposition in traces so you know if a request waited for other requests to fill a batch.
[08:23] [08:23] Priya Shah: how do you surface KV cache hits? we rely heavily on prefix caching for semantically similar prompts.
[08:29] Marcus Lee: KV cache hit rate is a field in the trace spans — we also give a cache heatmap over time. if you prefer we can export cache stats to your metrics backend.
[08:38] Karen Liu: from a security standpoint, if we do private deployment will the telemetry still be visible to Redwood support?
[08:45] Alicia Ramos: private gives you full control; Redwood support can access telemetry only with explicit consent and audit trails — we can contractually restrict access.
[08:55] [08:55] Marcus Lee: quick demo of the error analysis drilldown — selecting an error group shows representative requests, a delta in quality metrics, and a suggested remediation. some automations are labeled as beta.
[09:12] Daniel Brooks: beta concerns — we need production-grade automations. are the automations used for canary rollback GA?
[09:19] Marcus Lee: automated rollback and alerting for regressions are GA. some other convenience automations are beta but we can provide runbook templates.
[09:29] Priya Shah: ok, timeline — we want to pilot in Q3 with 2 routes and then scale. is that feasible?
[09:36] Alicia Ramos: absolutely, typical pilot is 2-4 weeks for baseline benchmarking then 6-8 weeks to expand and tune. we'll propose a pilot plan.
[09:44] [09:44] Marcus Lee: now request logs export — here's the configuration panel to set S3 bucket, encryption, and retention. note: for on-prem we provide an agent to forward logs.
[09:58] Karen Liu: do you support customer-managed keys per-bucket?
[10:02] Marcus Lee: yes per-bucket KMS is supported; we also have HSM options for Private.
[10:09] [10:09] Priya Shah: small question: do you capture user-provided function/tool calls in traces? we use function calling in a few routes.
[10:18] Marcus Lee: function calls are captured as spans and we show the payload (redacted if needed).
[10:24] Daniel Brooks: any gotchas around tokenization when switching quantized variants?
[10:29] Marcus Lee: tokenizers are consistent across variants but micro differences can appear for subword splits in corner cases; the console flags those under "tokenization delta" in the error tab.
[10:40] [10:40] Speaker 1: (background noise)
[10:45] Marcus Lee: ok, time check — 30 minutes left? actually we started at 15:00 so we have about 32 left — oh sorry math, we have about 32.
[10:55] Alicia Ramos: quick interjection — we'll also send the Dedicated SKU and pricing tiers, and include the enterprise retention add-on.
[11:03] Priya Shah: thanks. for the pilot we need data residency guarantee and proof of SOC2 controls.
[11:09] Alicia Ramos: noted, we'll send the SOC2 pack and architecture doc.
[11:15] Marcus Lee: last demo piece — request logs debugging flow: search for trace id, open full request, click link to model-run timeline, jump to the exact token with the issue, and open the correlated logs that show upstream service calls.
[11:33] Daniel Brooks: that correlates well with our microservices traces. we use Jaeger — any integrations?
[11:39] Marcus Lee: we can export trace spans to Jaeger-compatible backends and also send OTEL.
[11:45] Priya Shah: will you run a sample test on our corpus to show p95 numbers for both hosted and dedicated?
[11:52] Marcus Lee: yes we'll run the sample benchmarks and post results to the shared spreadsheet.
[11:58] [11:58] Speaker 2: (muted)
[12:00] Alicia Ramos: recap — key asks: security docs (SOC2 + KMS/HSM), pricing + Dedicated SKUs, pilot plan and benchmark run, and request logs export details. anyone disagree?
[12:13] Priya Shah: no, that's accurate.
[12:16] Daniel Brooks: agrees.
[12:18] Karen Liu: agree.
